NeoXider MCP Hub

One tool in your prompt instead of every schema.
MCP servers and skills in one lazy, human-approved
catalog — for any MCP client.

Quick start ·
Connect a client ·
One catalog ·
Measured results ·
How it compares ·
Changelog
Every MCP server you configure puts all of its tool schemas into every prompt, whether or not the ta
sk touches a tool. Ten servers can cost roughly 15,000 tokens before the model has read your questio
n, and a crowded tool list makes the model pick worse.
NeoXider MCP Hub is a stdio MCP server that exposes **one** tool, `capability_hub`. The model search
es a lightweight catalog, inspects permissions, wakes the one server it needs, calls it, and shuts i
t down again. Skills live in the same catalog and are loaded one at a time, only when selected.

| **One resident tool** | The host carries about 420 tokens, however many servers you configure. |
|
**MCP servers and skills together** | One catalog, one `search`, one trust model. Servers start on

demand; skill bodies load one at a time. |
| **Stopped, not just hidden** | A capability is a proces

s that is off until the model asks for it. `disable` stops it. |
| **Human approval** | A model can

*propose* a server or a skill. Only a person, outside the model, can approve it. |
| **Any MCP clien

t** | A plain stdio server: OpenCode, Claude Code, Claude Desktop, Cursor, DeepSeek Harness. |
| **M
easured, including the losses** | Context, accuracy, a head-to-head and a dynamic proof are reproduc
ible scripts in `bench/` — the one where Tool Search wins is published too. |
Left: every schema resident, every turn. Right: one tool, and the rest wakes on demand.

ub process.

## Quick start
Requirements: Node.js 22.19+ and pnpm.
[代码示例省略，未执行]
The default catalog contains only a bundled echo MCP and an example ML skill. Tests do not download
or execute third-party packages.
The client takes simple requests as plain flags (`--action`, `--query`, `--kind`, `--name`, `--tool`
). A request with arguments goes in a file, `pnpm client -- --input request.json`, because Windows P
owerShell 5.1 strips the double quotes from inline JSON passed with `--json`.

### DeepSeek Harness
Install the published bundle — no paths to edit, no build on your machine:
[代码示例省略，未执行]
Restart Harness. The hub runs inside the host process as one native model-facing tool, `capability_h
ub`. The catalog and state default to the installed package's `data/` directory; to keep them elsewh
ere, set the row's `catalogPath` / `stateDir` Config in your profile's `cordis.patch.yml`. `toolCall
TimeoutMs` raises the per-call ceiling from its 300,000 ms default, and `pageChars` sets the page si
eoutMs` raises the per-call ceiling from its 300,000 ms default, and `pageChars` sets the page size.
A built checkout loads the same way without packing it: insert the compiled entry by path. The plugi
n imports nothing from Harness at runtime, so it works from outside the profile's `node_modules`.
[代码示例省略，未执行]
Prefer the native tool with a local model. The alternative is a stdio child through the in-box MCP c
lient: build the hub, then merge `examples/dsh/cordis.patch.yml` into the active Harness Web profile
and adjust the absolute repository path. Harness then exposes the tool as `mcp__capability_hub__cap
ability_hub`, a long name that repeats itself. Small models sometimes misspell it, for example as `m
cp__capability-hub__…`, and a server that only recognizes declared tool names then returns the whole
call as plain text, so it never runs.
